overview: This House resolution, known as a 'rule,' sets the terms for House debate on four bills. Three concern the District of Columbia: H.R. 884, which would bar noncitizens from voting in D.C. local elections; H.R. 2056, which would require D.C. to comply with federal immigration laws; and H.R. 2096, which deals with how discipline for D.C. police officers is handled through union bargaining and how long the city has to bring disciplinary cases. The fourth, S. 331, a bill already passed by the Senate, deals with how fentanyl-related substances are classified under federal drug law. For each bill, the resolution allows one hour of debate, waives procedural objections, and permits no further amendments, only a single motion to recommit or commit. The House adopted it on June 10, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule moves several bills on public safety, elections, and fentanyl to the floor efficiently with set debate time for both sides.
against: Critics say bundling four separate bills and blocking amendments limits debate, and that three of the bills override decisions made by the District of Columbia's own local government.
